result.topic_en: Euler distinguishes three kinds of expressions in x and y: algebraic ones, ones involving differential ratios, and ones involving integral formulas. He then explains that the calculus of variations studies how such expressions change when the relation between x and y is altered infinitely little, through an arbitrary increment δy.

items.english: For the whole business comes down to this: if any relation between x and y is proposed and it is varied a little, or in its place some other relation between x and y is used that differs from it infinitely little in any way whatever, one must investigate how great a change all those expressions, of the first, second and third kinds, will undergo.
